knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility Decision
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decision task for a finite-domain constraint satisfaction instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I=(V,(D_x)_{x\in V},C)\) be a finite-domain CSP, where every \(D_x\) is finite and each constraint in \(C\) specifies an allowed relation on its scope. Define \[\operatorname{Sol}(I)=\{a\in\prod_{x\in V}D_x: a\text{ satisfies every }c\in C\}.\] The feasibility-decision task returns YES exactly when \(\operatorname{Sol}(I)\neq\varnothing\), and returns NO exactly when \(\operatorname{Sol}(I)=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Determine whether the finite-domain CSP has at least one assignment satisfying every constraint.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) and every domain \(D_x\) are finite.
Each constraint has a well-defined finite scope and satisfaction relation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I\text{ is feasible}\iff \operatorname{Sol}(I)\neq\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: set of satisfying assignments of the instance

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard finite-domain CSP decision-task definition
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically precise, matches the feasibility-decision leaf, and uses an appropriate content kind, but it has no inspectable citation. Standard-field rationale alone does not satisfy the requested source review.

knowledge_statements.title: Solution Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constructive search task for a finite-domain constraint satisfaction instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite-domain CSP \(I=(V,(D_x)_{x\in V},C)\), let \(\operatorname{Sol}(I)\) denote all assignments satisfying every constraint. The solution-search task must output some \(a\in\operatorname{Sol}(I)\) when this set is nonempty; if \(\operatorname{Sol}(I)=\varnothing\), it must output the distinguished result \(\mathsf{UNSAT}\). No particular satisfying assignment is preferred unless an additional ordering or objective is specified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Produce one satisfying assignment, or report that no satisfying assignment exists.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) and all variable domains are finite.
Constraint satisfaction is decidable for each complete assignment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{output}\in\operatorname{Sol}(I)\) if \(\operatorname{Sol}(I)\neq\varnothing\), and \(\text{output}=\mathsf{UNSAT}\) otherwise.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard constructive CSP task definition
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The constructive task is correctly distinguished from feasibility decision and enumeration, and definition is the appropriate content kind. No source with a specific locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Solution Enumeration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Duplicate-free enumeration of every solution of a finite-domain CSP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite-domain CSP \(I\), solution enumeration outputs a finite sequence \((a^1,\ldots,a^m)\) such that \[\{a^1,\ldots,a^m\}=\operatorname{Sol}(I)\quad\text{and}\quad a^i\neq a^j\text{ whenever }i\neq j.\] Thus every satisfying assignment appears exactly once and no nonsolution appears. The order of output is arbitrary unless the task specifies an ordering. When \(\operatorname{Sol}(I)=\varnothing\), the required sequence is empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: List every satisfying assignment exactly once, producing an empty list when none exists.
assumptions_latex: The CSP has finitely many variables, each with a finite domain.
Assignments and constraint satisfaction admit exact equality tests.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{a^1,\ldots,a^m\}=\operatorname{Sol}(I)\) with pairwise distinct outputs.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard exhaustive CSP task definition
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The duplicate-free exhaustive-output definition matches the exact leaf and is internally consistent, including the empty-solution case. It lacks an inspectable source citation.

knowledge_statements.title: Solution Counting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact counting task for finite-domain constraint satisfaction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite-domain CSP \(I=(V,(D_x)_{x\in V},C)\), the solution-counting task returns the nonnegative integer \[\#\operatorname{CSP}(I)=|\operatorname{Sol}(I)|=\sum_{a\in\prod_{x\in V}D_x}\mathbf{1}\{a\text{ satisfies every }c\in C\}.\] In particular, the returned value is zero exactly when the instance is infeasible. Distinct complete assignments are counted separately, even if they are related by a symmetry of the instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Return the exact number of complete assignments satisfying all constraints.
assumptions_latex: The variable set and every variable domain are finite.
Each complete assignment has a definite satisfaction status.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\#\operatorname{CSP}(I)=|\operatorname{Sol}(I)|\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}\).

notation.meaning: number of solutions of the instance

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard exact CSP counting definition
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact counting formulation and indicator expression correctly characterize this task, and definition fits the leaf. No source with a section, theorem, definition, or page locator is cited.

knowledge_statements.title: Boolean-Domain CSPs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite CSPs whose variables take Boolean values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A Boolean-domain CSP is a finite CSP \(I=(V,(D_x)_{x\in V},C)\) in which \(D_x=\{0,1\}\) for every \(x\in V\). Each constraint \(c\in C\) has an ordered scope \((x_1,\ldots,x_k)\) and a relation \(R_c\subseteq\{0,1\}^k\). An assignment \(a:V\to\{0,1\}\) satisfies \(c\) exactly when \((a(x_1),\ldots,a(x_k))\in R_c\), and it solves \(I\) when it satisfies all constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Boolean-domain CSP has only binary-valued variables and constraints represented by relations over Boolean tuples.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) and \(C\) are finite.
Every constraint has finite arity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Sol}(I)=\{a:V\to\{0,1\}:\forall c\in C,\ a|_{\operatorname{scope}(c)}\in R_c\}\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard relational definition of Boolean CSP
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The relational Boolean-domain specialization is precise and belongs in this definition leaf. It has no inspectable citation beyond standard-field rationale.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Symbolic-Domain CSPs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite CSPs over uninterpreted symbolic values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A finite symbolic-domain CSP is a finite CSP \(I=(V,(D_x)_{x\in V},C)\) in which every \(D_x\) is a finite set of symbols. The symbols carry no required numerical order or arithmetic interpretation. Each constraint \(c\) is specified by a relation \(R_c\subseteq\prod_{x\in\operatorname{scope}(c)}D_x\). A complete assignment \(a\in\prod_{x\in V}D_x\) is a solution exactly when its restriction to every constraint scope belongs to the corresponding relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Variables range over finite sets of labels, and relational constraints determine which symbolic tuples are allowed.
assumptions_latex: \(V\), \(C\), and every \(D_x\) are finite.
Domain symbols are compared by identity unless additional structure is declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a\in\operatorname{Sol}(I)\iff \forall c\in C,\ a|_{\operatorname{scope}(c)}\in R_c\).

notation.meaning: finite symbolic domain of variable x

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard relational finite-domain CSP definition specialized to symbols
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement consistently defines the symbolic regime as finite uninterpreted labels with relational constraints, and definition is the correct role. No source reference is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Integer-Domain CSPs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite CSPs whose variable domains are finite integer sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A finite integer-domain CSP is a finite CSP \(I=(V,(D_x)_{x\in V},C)\) with each domain satisfying \(D_x\subset\mathbb{Z}\) and \(|D_x|<\infty\). Constraints may be given extensionally as relations or intensionally as predicates over their integer-valued scopes. An assignment \(a\in\prod_{x\in V}D_x\) solves \(I\) exactly when every constraint predicate evaluates to true, equivalently when each scoped tuple lies in its allowed relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each variable ranges over a finite set of integers, and every stated constraint must hold.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) and \(C\) are finite.
Each \(D_x\) is a finite subset of \(\mathbb{Z}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Sol}(I)=\{a\in\prod_{x\in V}D_x:\forall c\in C,\ c(a)=\mathsf{true}\}\).

notation.meaning: finite integer domain of variable x
truth value of constraint c under assignment a

review_flags: source_scope_indirect: locator supports finite integer modeling but may not state the relational CSP definition

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The mathematical definition is coherent and fits the finite integer-domain CSP leaf, but the cited integer-programming chapter is only indirectly related and is not shown to support the relational CSP definition or its extensional/intensional formulation. A CSP-specific source is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Set-Domain CSPs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite CSPs whose values are subsets of fixed finite universes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A finite set-domain CSP is a finite CSP \(I=(V,(D_x)_{x\in V},C)\) in which every variable \(x\) has a finite universe \(U_x\) and a domain \(D_x\subseteq 2^{U_x}\). Thus an assignment chooses one admissible subset \(a(x)\in D_x\) for each variable. Each constraint is a relation on the selected subsets in its scope, and \(a\) is a solution exactly when every such relation contains the corresponding tuple of sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Variables take admissible subsets of finite universes, and constraints relate the selected sets.
assumptions_latex: \(V\), \(C\), and every universe \(U_x\) are finite.
Each domain \(D_x\) is a specified subset of \(2^{U_x}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a\in\operatorname{Sol}(I)\iff a(x)\in D_x\text{ for all }x\in V\text{ and every set constraint is satisfied}\).

notation.meaning: finite universe associated with variable x
admissible set values for variable x

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard finite set-variable CSP definition
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-universe power-set formulation correctly identifies the set-domain regime, and definition fits the leaf. It lacks a source with an inspectable locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Single-Objective Constraint Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite constraint optimization with one scalar objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) be a finite-domain CSP with feasible set \(F=\operatorname{Sol}(I)\), and let \(f:F\to T\), where \((T,\preceq)\) is totally ordered. A single-objective minimization problem seeks \(a^\star\in F\) satisfying \[f(a^\star)\preceq f(a)\qquad\text{for every }a\in F.\] If \(F=\varnothing\), the optimization problem is infeasible. Maximization is defined by reversing \(\preceq\). Ties are allowed: every feasible assignment attaining the best objective value is optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimize one totally ordered scalar criterion over all assignments satisfying the hard constraints.
assumptions_latex: The feasible set \(F\) is finite.
The objective is defined on every feasible assignment.
The objective codomain is totally ordered.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{a\in F}f(a)\), or the instance is infeasible when \(F=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: set of assignments satisfying all hard constraints

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard finite single-objective optimization definition
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite single-objective minimization definition is precise, handles infeasibility and ties, and uses the correct content kind. No inspectable source is cited.

knowledge_statements.title: Lexicographic Constraint Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite constraint optimization with priority-ordered objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the feasible set of a finite-domain CSP and let \(f=(f_1,\ldots,f_k):F\to T_1\times\cdots\times T_k\), where each \((T_i,\preceq_i)\) is totally ordered and lower values are preferred. Define \(f(a)\prec_{\mathrm{lex}}f(b)\) when, at the smallest index \(j\) with \(f_j(a)\neq f_j(b)\), one has \(f_j(a)\prec_j f_j(b)\). A feasible assignment \(a^\star\) is lexicographically optimal when no \(a\in F\) satisfies \(f(a)\prec_{\mathrm{lex}}f(a^\star)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize objectives in priority order, using later objectives only to break ties in earlier ones.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is finite and nonempty.
The number \(k\) of objectives is finite.
Every objective codomain is totally ordered.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a^\star\in F\) and \(\nexists a\in F:\ f(a)\prec_{\mathrm{lex}}f(a^\star)\).

notation.meaning: objectives ordered from highest to lowest priority

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The priority-ordered lexicographic definition is mathematically consistent and appropriate for this objective-structure leaf. It has no source reference with a specific locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Pareto Constraint Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite multiobjective optimization under componentwise dominance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the feasible set of a finite-domain CSP and let \(f=(f_1,\ldots,f_k):F\to T_1\times\cdots\times T_k\), with every objective minimized over a totally ordered set. An assignment \(a\in F\) dominates \(b\in F\) when \(f_i(a)\preceq_i f_i(b)\) for every \(i\) and \(f_j(a)\prec_j f_j(b)\) for at least one \(j\). A feasible assignment is Pareto optimal exactly when no other feasible assignment dominates it; all such assignments form the Pareto set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible assignment is Pareto optimal when no feasible alternative improves one objective without worsening another.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is finite and nonempty.
There are finitely many objectives.
Every objective codomain is totally ordered.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P=\{a\in F:\nexists b\in F\text{ such that }b\text{ dominates }a\}\).
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The componentwise dominance and Pareto-set definition matches the exact leaf, with consistent plain text and LaTeX. No inspectable citation is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Maximum CSP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unweighted maximization of satisfied constraints over complete assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A Maximum CSP instance consists of finite variables \(V\), finite domains \((D_x)_{x\in V}\), and a finite multiset of constraints \(C\). Every complete assignment \(a\in\prod_{x\in V}D_x\) receives value \[\operatorname{val}(a)=\sum_{c\in C}\mathbf{1}\{a\text{ satisfies }c\}.\] The task is to find \(a^\star\) maximizing \(\operatorname{val}(a)\). Equivalently, \(a^\star\) minimizes the number \(|C|-\operatorname{val}(a)\) of violated constraints. Repeated constraints contribute according to multiplicity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Find a complete assignment satisfying as many unweighted constraints as possible.
assumptions_latex: The variable set, domains, and constraint multiset are finite.
Each constraint has unit contribution when satisfied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a^\star\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{a\in\prod_{x\in V}D_x}\sum_{c\in C}\mathbf{1}\{a\text{ satisfies }c\}\).

notation.meaning: number of constraints satisfied by assignment a

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard unweighted Maximum CSP definition
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The unweighted Maximum CSP formulation correctly maximizes the number of satisfied constraints and appropriately treats repeated constraints by multiplicity. Definition fits the leaf, but no source with a specific locator is cited.

knowledge_statements.title: Weighted CSP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive, minimization-form weighted constraint satisfaction over finite domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A weighted CSP consists of finite-domain variables \(X=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\), scopes \(S_1,\ldots,S_m\), and cost functions \(w_j:\prod_{x_i\in S_j}D_i\to\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}\cup\{+\infty\}\). For a complete assignment \(a\in\prod_{i=1}^nD_i\), its cost is \(W(a)=\sum_{j=1}^m w_j(a|_{S_j})\). The problem is to find \(a^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{a}W(a)\). A tuple assigned cost \(+\infty\) is forbidden; the instance is feasible precisely when some assignment has finite total cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weighted CSP minimizes the sum of local nonnegative costs over finite-domain assignments, with infinite cost representing a forbidden tuple.
assumptions_latex: \(n,m<\infty\) and every domain \(D_i\) is finite and nonempty.
Costs are combined additively and compared by minimization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{a\in\prod_iD_i}\sum_{j=1}^m w_j(a|_{S_j})\).

notation.meaning: restriction of assignment a to scope S_j

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The additive minimization definition fits the Weighted CSP leaf and is mathematically coherent, but no inspectable citation supports the selected cost domain, infinity convention, or precise formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Valued CSP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-domain VCSP in the standard additive cost-function formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A valued CSP instance consists of finite-domain variables \(X=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\) and valued constraints \((S_j,f_j)\), where \(f_j:\prod_{x_i\in S_j}D_i\to\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_{\ge0}\) and \(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_{\ge0}=\mathbb{Q}_{\ge0}\cup\{+\infty\}\). The value of an assignment \(a\in\prod_iD_i\) is \(F(a)=\sum_j f_j(a|_{S_j})\), and solving the instance means computing an assignment minimizing \(F\). Finite-valued languages exclude \(+\infty\); general-valued languages may use it to encode hard constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valued CSP minimizes a sum of rational-valued local cost functions; infinite values may encode hard constraints.
assumptions_latex: Every variable domain \(D_i\) and the constraint family are finite.
The optimization convention is minimization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Opt}(I)=\min_{a\in\prod_iD_i}\sum_j f_j(a|_{S_j})\).

notation.meaning: local valued constraint or cost function
nonnegative rationals extended by positive infinity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and additive VCSP formulation fit the leaf, but the record has no citation for the rational codomain or the finite-valued versus general-valued terminology.

knowledge_statements.title: Semiring-Based CSP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Soft CSP defined over a commutative semiring of preference values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=(A,\oplus,\otimes,\mathbf{0},\mathbf{1})\) be a commutative semiring. A semiring-based CSP consists of finite-domain variables and constraints \(c_j:\prod_{x_i\in S_j}D_i\to A\). Each complete assignment \(a\) receives aggregate value \(V(a)=\bigotimes_j c_j(a|_{S_j})\). The induced preference order is \(u\preceq_S v\) exactly when \(u\oplus v=v\). A solution is an assignment whose aggregate value is maximal under \(\preceq_S\); if maximal values are incomparable, the solution set contains every undominated assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A semiring-based CSP combines local preference values multiplicatively and compares aggregate values using the order induced by semiring addition.
assumptions_latex: \((A,\oplus,\mathbf{0})\) and \((A,\otimes,\mathbf{1})\) satisfy the commutative-semiring axioms.
Every domain and the constraint family are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a^*\) is a solution if no assignment \(b\) satisfies \(V(a^*)\prec_S V(b)\).

notation.meaning: choice operation inducing the preference order
aggregate semiring value of assignment a

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A generic commutative semiring does not ensure that u preceq_S v iff u opplus v=v defines the stated preference order; idempotence and the precise c-semiring axiom variant must be established by an authoritative source.

children.title: Incumbent Certificates
children.top_down_role: Evidence attached to candidate objective values and recorded solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal certificate supplied by a currently best-known feasible assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite-domain minimization problem with feasible set \(F\) and objective \(f:F\to\mathbb{R}\), an incumbent certificate is a complete assignment \(\hat a\), together with its claimed value \(U\). Verification recomputes every domain-membership and constraint predicate on \(\hat a\), recomputes \(f(\hat a)\), and accepts exactly when \(\hat a\in F\) and \(U=f(\hat a)\). Acceptance certifies the valid upper bound \(f^*\le U\), where \(f^*=\min_{a\in F}f(a)\); it does not by itself certify optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A verified feasible incumbent and its recomputed objective value certify an upper bound for a minimization problem, but not optimality.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is finite and all constraints and objective values are exactly evaluable.
The problem uses the minimization convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\hat a\in F\) and \(U=f(\hat a)\) imply \(f^*\le U\).

children.title: Feasibility Certificates
children.top_down_role: Evidence establishing satisfaction of the modeled constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct witness certificate for finite-domain constraint feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For variables \(x_i\in D_i\) and constraints \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\), a feasibility certificate is a complete tuple \(a=(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\). A verifier accepts it exactly when \(a_i\in D_i\) for every \(i\) and \(C_j(a|_{S_j})=\mathrm{true}\) for every \(j\). Acceptance certifies that the feasible set \(F=\{x\in\prod_iD_i:C_j(x|_{S_j})\text{ holds for all }j\}\) is nonempty. Rejection of one tuple does not certify infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A complete assignment is a feasibility certificate when every domain check and every constraint evaluation succeeds.
assumptions_latex: Every domain \(D_i\) is explicitly represented and finite.
Each constraint predicate \(C_j\) is exactly evaluable on a complete local tuple.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a_i\in D_i\) for all \(i\) and \(C_j(a|_{S_j})\) for all \(j\) imply \(F\ne\varnothing\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The direct witness formulation is correct and the certificate content kind fits the leaf, but no inspectable source is supplied for the verifier-based definition.

children.title: Incumbent Feasibility Validation
children.top_down_role: Structural checks connecting an incumbent record to its feasibility evidence.

knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Feasibility Validation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic validation procedure for a proposed incumbent assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a finite-domain constraint optimization instance and a proposed incumbent \((\hat a,U)\). First check \(\hat a_i\in D_i\) for every variable. Next evaluate each constraint \(C_j(\hat a|_{S_j})\); stop and return invalid at the first failure. If all constraints hold, compute \(v=f(\hat a)\) and compare it with \(U\) under the instance's exact numeric convention. Return valid with certified value \(v\) exactly when the comparison succeeds; otherwise return value-mismatch. A valid result establishes primal feasibility and the corresponding incumbent bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Validate an incumbent by checking domains and constraints, then independently recomputing and comparing its objective value.
assumptions_latex: All domains, constraints, and objective terms are deterministically evaluable.
Objective comparison uses an explicitly specified exact representation or sound tolerance rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Validate}(\hat a,U)=\mathrm{valid}\) implies \(\hat a\in F\) and \(U=f(\hat a)\).

notation.meaning: proposed incumbent and claimed objective value

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The deterministic validation procedure and algorithm content kind match the leaf, but no source supports the exact validation contract, including the numeric comparison convention and returned guarantees.

children.title: Bound Certificates
children.top_down_role: Evidence supporting lower or upper objective bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Verifiable global lower or upper bounds for finite-domain optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem \(f^*=\min_{a\in F}f(a)\), a lower-bound certificate is data \(y\) from which a verifier establishes \(L(y)\le f(a)\) for every \(a\in F\), hence \(L(y)\le f^*\). A feasible assignment \(\hat a\in F\) gives the upper-bound certificate \(U=f(\hat a)\), hence \(f^*\le U\). Thus accepted certificates bracket the optimum as \(L\le f^*\le U\). The derivation encoded by \(y\) may use an exact relaxation, decomposition, or exhaustive partition, but each inference must be independently checkable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Verified lower- and upper-bound witnesses bracket the optimal value of a finite-domain minimization problem.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is finite and the objective is minimized.
The verifier checks every inference used to derive \(L\) and directly validates the incumbent defining \(U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L\le f^*\le U\).

children.title: Optimality Certificates
children.top_down_role: Evidence supporting the optimal status of a feasible solution.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimality Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Paired primal and bound evidence proving global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f^*=\min_{a\in F}f(a)\), an optimality certificate comprises a feasible assignment \(\hat a\), its verified value \(U=f(\hat a)\), and a verified global lower-bound certificate establishing \(L\le f(a)\) for every \(a\in F\). If \(L=U\), then \(L\le f^*\le U\) forces \(f(\hat a)=f^*=L=U\), so \(\hat a\) is globally optimal. With tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\), the condition \(U-L\le\varepsilon\) instead certifies additive \(\varepsilon\)-optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible incumbent and a matching global lower bound certify exact optimality; a bounded gap certifies additive approximate optimality.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a finite-domain minimization problem.
Primal feasibility, the incumbent value, and the global lower bound are independently verified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L=U\) implies \(\hat a\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{a\in F}f(a)\); \(U-L\le\varepsilon\) implies \(f(\hat a)-f^*\le\varepsilon\).

children.title: Bound Closure for Optimality
children.top_down_role: The relationship between incumbent values, objective bounds, and certified optimality.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound Closure for Optimality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality follows when certified primal and dual bounds close.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a finite-domain minimization problem with optimal value \(f^*\). Suppose a valid incumbent provides an upper bound \(U\), while a sound bounding procedure provides a nondecreasing sequence \((L_k)\) of certified global lower bounds. For every \(k\), \(L_k\le f^*\le U\). If some \(k\) satisfies \(L_k=U\), the incumbent is globally optimal. More generally, termination at \(U-L_k\le\varepsilon\) certifies additive \(\varepsilon\)-optimality. Exact closure requires bounds and objective values to use mutually consistent numerical representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When a certified lower bound reaches the incumbent value, the incumbent is optimal; a residual gap bounds additive suboptimality.
assumptions_latex: Each \(L_k\) is a certified global lower bound and \(U\) comes from a certified feasible incumbent.
The optimization convention is minimization and \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_k=U\Rightarrow f^*=U\), and \(U-L_k\le\varepsilon\Rightarrow U-f^*\le\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: certified lower bound at stage k

knowledge_statements.title: Quantified CSP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-domain constraints with an ordered existential-universal quantifier prefix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A quantified CSP is a sentence \(Q_1x_1\,Q_2x_2\cdots Q_nx_n\;\bigwedge_{j=1}^m C_j(x|_{S_j})\), where every \(D_i\) is finite, each \(Q_i\in\{\exists,\forall\}\), and each constraint \(C_j\) is a relation over the variables in \(S_j\). The instance is true when the existential player has a strategy assigning each existential variable as a function of preceding universal choices such that every constraint holds for every play consistent with that strategy. Ordinary CSP is the special case in which all quantifiers are existential.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quantified CSP asks whether existential choices can satisfy all constraints against every sequence of universally quantified finite-domain choices.
assumptions_latex: The quantifier order is fixed and every variable domain \(D_i\) is finite and nonempty.
Each constraint is evaluated on a complete assignment to its scope.

notation.meaning: existential or universal quantifier for variable x_i

knowledge_statements.title: Dynamic CSP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sequence of related CSP instances that changes over time.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A dynamic CSP is an indexed sequence \((I_t)_{t\in T}\), where each \(I_t=(X_t,D_t,C_t)\) is a finite-domain CSP and a transition from \(I_t\) to \(I_{t+1}\) may add, remove, or modify variables, domains, or constraints. At time \(t\), a solution is an assignment \(a_t\in\prod_{x_i\in X_t}D_{i,t}\) satisfying every constraint in \(C_t\). A dynamic solution process maintains or recomputes such assignments after each disclosed transition; optional change costs are additional modeling data, not part of feasibility itself.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dynamic CSP is a time-indexed family of finite CSPs whose variables, domains, or constraints may change between stages.
assumptions_latex: Each stage \(I_t\) has finitely many variables, finite nonempty domains, and finitely many constraints.
Transitions are disclosed before a solution for the new stage is required.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a_t\) solves stage \(t\) exactly when \(C(a_t)=\mathrm{true}\) for every \(C\in C_t\).

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed CSP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-domain CSP whose information and variable control are distributed among agents.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A distributed CSP consists of finite-domain variables \(X\), constraints \(C\), agents \(P\), an ownership map \(o:X\to P\), and a specification of which agents know each constraint. Agent \(p\) selects values only for variables in \(o^{-1}(p)\) and communicates according to the permitted interaction model. A global solution is an assignment \(a\in\prod_iD_i\) satisfying every constraint in \(C\), regardless of how ownership or knowledge is partitioned. The distributed problem is to obtain such an assignment through agent-local computation and permitted communication.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A distributed CSP partitions variable control and constraint information among agents, which must jointly obtain a globally satisfying assignment.
assumptions_latex: The agent, variable, domain, and constraint sets are finite.
Every variable has one designated owner, and the communication model is specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a\) is a global solution exactly when \(C(a|_{S_C})=\mathrm{true}\) for every \(C\in C\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A compressed table representation of a constraint relation \(C\subseteq U\) is an encoding \(E\) together with an exact decoding rule \(\operatorname{dec}\) satisfying \(\operatorname{dec}(E)=C\). children.title: Grammar-Defined Relations

knowledge_statements.title: Grammar-Defined Relations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Language-based representation of a finite-domain relation using an explicit tuple encoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D_1,\ldots,D_n\) be finite domains, let \(\Sigma\) be a finite alphabet, and let \(\operatorname{enc}:D_1\times\cdots\times D_n\to\Sigma^*\) be an injective encoding. A grammar \(G\) over \(\Sigma\) defines the relation
\[
R_G=\{(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\in D_1\times\cdots\times D_n:\operatorname{enc}(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\in L(G)\}.
\]
Thus a tuple satisfies the grammar-defined constraint exactly when its encoded word is generated by \(G\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A grammar defines precisely those finite-domain tuples whose encoded words belong to the grammar's language.

children.title: Decision-Diagram Relations

knowledge_statements.title: Decision-Diagram Relations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Layered decision-diagram representation of an ordered finite-domain relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D_1,\ldots,D_n\) be finite domains. A layered decision diagram has a root in layer \(0\), a terminal in layer \(n\), and arcs from layer \(i-1\) to layer \(i\) labelled by elements of \(D_i\). It represents
\[
R_B=\{(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\in D_1\times\cdots\times D_n:\text{a root-to-terminal path has successive labels }a_1,\ldots,a_n\}.
\]
Merging nodes with identical accepted suffix sets preserves \(R_B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tuple belongs to the relation exactly when its values label a root-to-terminal path through the layered decision diagram.

Layer \(i\) arcs are labelled from \(D_i\).

children.title: Logical Constraint Forms
children.top_down_role: Logical composition retained at the constraint-model layer; SAT normalization and proof systems are external dependencies.

knowledge_statements.title: Full Reification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact Boolean encoding of a finite-domain constraint's truth value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C(x)\) be a constraint over a finite-domain tuple \(x\), and let \(b\in\{0,1\}\). The full reification of \(C\) by \(b\) is
\[
b=1\;\Longleftrightarrow\;C(x).
\]
Equivalently, it is the conjunction \((b=1\Rightarrow C(x))\land(C(x)\Rightarrow b=1)\). Hence every satisfying assignment sets \(b\) to the unique Boolean truth value of \(C(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Full reification makes a Boolean variable true exactly when the associated constraint is satisfied.
assumptions_latex: \(x\) ranges over a finite Cartesian product.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard equivalence semantics of full constraint reification
No supplied source locator directly supports constraint reification.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The equivalence correctly describes full reification and the definition kind fits, but no inspectable source locator supports the constraint-programming terminology.

children.title: Half Reification
children.top_down_role: One-directional links between a Boolean indicator and a constraint.

knowledge_statements.title: Half Reification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-way Boolean activation of a finite-domain constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C(x)\) be a constraint over a finite-domain tuple \(x\), and let \(b\in\{0,1\}\). The positive half reification of \(C\) by \(b\) is
\[
b=1\;\Longrightarrow\;C(x).
\]
It requires \(C(x)\) whenever \(b=1\), but imposes no converse: an assignment may satisfy \(C(x)\) while having \(b=0\). The opposite-direction half reification is \(C(x)\Rightarrow b=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Half reification enforces only one implication between a Boolean indicator and a constraint, so the indicator need not equal the constraint's truth value.
assumptions_latex: \(x\) ranges over a finite Cartesian product.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Positive half reification is \(b=1\Rightarrow C(x)\), without the converse.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard one-implication semantics of half reification
No supplied source locator directly supports half reification.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two possible one-way implications are stated consistently and the definition fits the leaf, but no inspectable source supports the terminology and directional convention for half reification.

children.title: Implicational Constraints
children.top_down_role: Constraint forms governed by a directed logical implication.

knowledge_statements.title: Implicational Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical implication between finite-domain constraint predicates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For constraint predicates \(P(x)\) and \(Q(x)\) on the same finite-domain assignment space \(X\), the implicational constraint \(P(x)\Rightarrow Q(x)\) denotes
\[
\{x\in X:\neg P(x)\lor Q(x)\}.
\]
Consequently, an assignment violates the constraint exactly when \(P(x)\) is true and \(Q(x)\) is false; assignments with a false antecedent satisfy it vacuously.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An implicational constraint excludes exactly those assignments satisfying its antecedent while violating its consequent.
assumptions_latex: \(P,Q:X\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P(x)\Rightarrow Q(x)\equiv\neg P(x)\lor Q(x)\).
review_flags: No supplied source locator directly supports implicational constraints.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The classical implication semantics are precise and fit the leaf, but the record provides no inspectable source for its use as a finite-domain constraint form.

children.title: Reification Directionality
children.top_down_role: Forward, reverse, and asymmetric linkage regimes for reified constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Reification Directionality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical distinction among forward, reverse, and bidirectional reification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a Boolean variable \(b\) and constraint \(C(x)\), define the forward channel \(F=(b=1\Rightarrow C(x))\) and reverse channel \(R=(C(x)\Rightarrow b=1)\). Neither \(F\) nor \(R\) implies the other in general. Their conjunction is full reification:
\[
F\land R\;\Longleftrightarrow\;(b=1\Longleftrightarrow C(x)).
\]
Thus propagation or modeling based on only one direction cannot generally infer the converse direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Forward and reverse reification are independent one-way conditions; imposing both yields full reification.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a Boolean-valued constraint predicate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\land R\equiv(b=1\Longleftrightarrow C(x))\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: propositional decomposition of logical equivalence
No supplied source locator directly supports reification directionality.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The forward/reverse decomposition is mathematically correct and property is the appropriate kind, but no source locator supports the reification-directionality terminology or modeling claim.

knowledge_statements.title: Boolean Reification Channels
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boolean variables linked exactly to the truth values of multiple constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C_1(x),\ldots,C_m(x)\) be constraints and let \(b_1,\ldots,b_m\in\{0,1\}\). A Boolean reification channel imposes
\[
\bigwedge_{i=1}^{m}\bigl(b_i=1\Longleftrightarrow C_i(x)\bigr).
\]
For every assignment to \(x\), the channel uniquely determines \(b_i=\mathbf{1}[C_i(x)]\). Consequently any Boolean formula \(\varphi(b_1,\ldots,b_m)\) represents the corresponding logical composition obtained by substituting \(C_i(x)\) for \(b_i=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reification channel equates Boolean variables with constraint truth values, allowing Boolean formulas to represent logical compositions of constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(m\) is finite.
\(b_i\in\{0,1\}\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b_i=\mathbf{1}[C_i(x)]\) for all \(i\).

No supplied source locator directly supports Boolean reification channels.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The componentwise full-reification representation is coherent, but no inspectable source supports the named Boolean-channel construction and its substitution interpretation.

knowledge_statements.title: Conjunctive Constraint Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible set represented as an intersection of finite-domain constraint relations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X=D_1\times\cdots\times D_n\) be a finite assignment space and let \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\) be predicates on \(X\). The conjunctive model
\[
C_1(x)\land\cdots\land C_m(x)
\]
has feasible set
\[
F=\bigcap_{j=1}^{m}\{x\in X:C_j(x)\}.
\]
Thus an assignment is feasible exactly when it satisfies every constituent constraint; one violated conjunct makes it infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conjunctive model accepts exactly the assignments satisfying every constituent constraint, so its feasible set is their intersection.
assumptions_latex: \(D_1,\ldots,D_n\) and \(m\) are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in F\Longleftrightarrow\bigwedge_{j=1}^{m}C_j(x)\).

notation.meaning: feasible set of the conjunctive model

knowledge_statements.title: Disjunctive Constraint Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible set represented as a union of alternative finite-domain relations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X=D_1\times\cdots\times D_n\) be a finite assignment space and let \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\) be predicates on \(X\). The disjunctive model
\[
C_1(x)\lor\cdots\lor C_m(x)
\]
has feasible set
\[
F=\bigcup_{j=1}^{m}\{x\in X:C_j(x)\}.
\]
Thus an assignment is feasible exactly when it satisfies at least one alternative; the alternatives need not be mutually exclusive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A disjunctive model accepts assignments satisfying at least one alternative constraint, so its feasible set is the union of the alternatives.
assumptions_latex: \(D_1,\ldots,D_n\) and \(m\) are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in F\Longleftrightarrow\bigvee_{j=1}^{m}C_j(x)\).

notation.meaning: feasible set of the disjunctive model

children.title: Conditional Constraints
children.top_down_role: Constraint structures selected according to a condition.

knowledge_statements.title: Conditional Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: If-then-else selection between two finite-domain constraint predicates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g(x)\) be a Boolean-valued condition and let \(C_1(x)\) and \(C_0(x)\) be constraint predicates on a finite assignment space \(X\). The conditional constraint “if \(g\) then \(C_1\), else \(C_0\)” is
\[
(g(x)\Rightarrow C_1(x))\land(\neg g(x)\Rightarrow C_0(x)).
\]
Its satisfying set is \((G\cap R_1)\cup((X\setminus G)\cap R_0)\), where \(G,R_1,R_0\) are the truth sets of \(g,C_1,C_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conditional constraint enforces one constraint when its condition is true and another when the condition is false.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite assignment space.
\(g,C_1,C_0\) are Boolean-valued predicates on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_{\mathrm{if}}\equiv(g\Rightarrow C_1)\land(\neg g\Rightarrow C_0)\).

notation.meaning: truth sets of g, C_1, and C_0

children.title: Guarded Constraints
children.top_down_role: Constraints controlled by an explicit activation guard.

knowledge_statements.title: Guarded Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint activated only when a Boolean guard holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g(x)\) be a Boolean-valued guard and \(C(x)\) a constraint predicate on a finite assignment space \(X\). The guarded constraint \(g:C\) has semantics
\[
g(x)\Rightarrow C(x),
\]
with satisfying set \((X\setminus G)\cup(G\cap R_C)\), where \(G=\{x:g(x)\}\) and \(R_C=\{x:C(x)\}\). Hence the constraint is vacuously satisfied when the guard is false and enforces \(C\) when the guard is true.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A guarded constraint enforces its body when the guard is true and is vacuously satisfied when the guard is false.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite assignment space.
\(g,C:X\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_{g:C}=(X\setminus G)\cup(G\cap R_C)\).

notation.meaning: relation defined by the guarded constraint

children.title: Guard Activation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Positive, negative, and multiway activation structures for guarded modeling.

knowledge_statements.title: Guard Activation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Three-valued classification of a guarded constraint under a partial assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p\) be a partial assignment, let \(\operatorname{Ext}(p)\) be its total extensions, and let \(g\) guard a constraint \(C\). The guard is active at \(p\) if \(g(x)\) holds for every \(x\in\operatorname{Ext}(p)\), inactive if it fails for every such \(x\), and undetermined otherwise. In the active regime the guarded constraint reduces to \(C\); in the inactive regime it is satisfied independently of \(C\); in the undetermined regime both guarded alternatives remain possible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under a partial assignment, a guard is active, inactive, or undetermined according to whether all, none, or some compatible completions satisfy it.
assumptions_latex: \(p\) has at least one total extension.
\(g\) is Boolean-valued on total assignments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Ext}(p)\subseteq G\), \(\operatorname{Ext}(p)\cap G=\varnothing\), or both intersections are nonempty, respectively.

notation.meaning: set of total extensions of p

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Model Channeling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact channeling between two finite-domain representations of the same solution object.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F_X\subseteq D_X\) and \(F_Y\subseteq D_Y\) be the feasible assignments of two finite-domain models, and let \(\phi:F_X\to S\) and \(\psi:F_Y\to S\) interpret assignments as objects in a common set \(S\). A channeling relation \(C\subseteq D_X\times D_Y\) is exact when
\[
(F_X\times F_Y)\cap C=\{(x,y)\in F_X\times F_Y:\phi(x)=\psi(y)\},
\]
and both coordinate projections of this set are respectively \(F_X\) and \(F_Y\). The channeled dual model consists of both constraint systems together with \((x,y)\in C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact channeling couples precisely those feasible assignments of two models that represent the same object, without eliminating any feasible assignment of either model.
assumptions_latex: \(D_X\) and \(D_Y\) are finite Cartesian products.
\(\phi(F_X)=\psi(F_Y)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((F_X\times F_Y)\cap C=\{(x,y):\phi(x)=\psi(y)\}\), with projections \(F_X\) and \(F_Y\).

notation.meaning: Feasible assignment sets of the two models.
Common set of represented solution objects.

knowledge_statements.title: Derived Variable Views
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Functional views that expose transformed values without introducing independent choices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x\) be a finite-domain variable with domain \(D\), and let \(f:D\to E\) be a total function. A derived variable view \(y=f(x)\) has domain \(f(D)\) and is constrained by
\[
y=v\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x\in f^{-1}(\{v\})
\]
for every \(v\in f(D)\). Any constraint \(R(y,z_1,\ldots,z_k)\) using the view denotes \(R(f(x),z_1,\ldots,z_k)\). Thus assigning \(x=a\) uniquely determines \(y=f(a)\), while restricting \(y\) to \(B\subseteq f(D)\) restricts \(x\) to \(f^{-1}(B)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A derived view represents a deterministic function of another variable; constraints and domain restrictions on the view are interpreted through that function and its preimages.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is finite.
\(f:D\to E\) is total.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D(y)=f(D)\) and \(y=f(x)\) under every admissible assignment.

authoritative constraint-programming source locator not supplied
