knowledge_statements.statement_plain: MiniZinc rejects an argument, assignment, or result whose type cannot reach the required type through a unique permitted implicit coercion.
knowledge_statements.title: Coercion Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits, but the claims about structural coercions, uniqueness, ambiguity, and overload resolution require a precise MiniZinc specification citation.

children.title: Predicate Declarations
children.top_down_role: Reusable constraint-bearing declarations with typed parameters.

assumptions_latex: Each formal parameter has a declared MiniZinc type-instantiation.
The predicate body is a well-typed Boolean expression in the formal parameters and visible declarations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A predicate call denotes the body with actual arguments substituted for formal parameters and contributes the resulting Boolean constraint.
review_flags: Authoritative MiniZinc specification locator required for declaration syntax, scoping, and overload details.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Declarative semantics of user-defined MiniZinc predicates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A predicate declaration introduces a name \(p\), formal parameters \((u_1,\ldots,u_k)\), and a Boolean body \(B(u_1,ldots,u_k)\). A call \(p(a_1,\ldots,a_k)\) is admissible when every actual argument \(a_i\) is type-instantiation compatible with \(u_i\). Its logical meaning is \(B(a_1,\ldots,a_k)\), with parameters bound to the actual arguments according to MiniZinc scoping rules. Thus posting the call requires \(B(a_1,\ldots,a_k)\) to hold; the declaration does not introduce mutable state or an independently chosen return value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A predicate declaration names a typed Boolean model fragment; a well-typed call contributes that fragment as a constraint with actual arguments substituted.
knowledge_statements.title: Predicate Declarations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits, but declaration, binding, and call semantics lack a specification source. The body notation also contains “ldots” instead of “\ldots”.

children.title: Function Declarations
children.top_down_role: Reusable value-producing declarations within MiniZinc models.

assumptions_latex: Formal parameters and the declared result have well-formed MiniZinc type-instantiations.
The function body is well typed in its declaration scope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A well-typed function call denotes the body evaluated or instantiated with its formal parameters bound to the actual arguments.
review_flags: Authoritative MiniZinc specification locator required for function restrictions, overloading, and partiality semantics.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Typed, expression-valued MiniZinc function declarations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A function declaration introduces a result type-instantiation \(\rho\), a name \(f\), formal parameters \((u_1,\ldots,u_k)\), and a body expression \(E(u_1,\ldots,u_k)\). A call \(f(a_1,\ldots,a_k)\) is admissible when each \(a_i\) is compatible with \(u_i\) and the type-instantiation of \(E\) is compatible with \(\rho\). The call denotes \(E(a_1,\ldots,a_k)\) under lexical parameter binding. Unlike a predicate call, it yields a value or decision expression of result type-instantiation \(\rho\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A function declaration names a typed expression; each well-typed call substitutes actual arguments into the body and yields a result of the declared type-instantiation.
knowledge_statements.title: Function Declarations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits, but MiniZinc function typing, binding, result-instantiation, and possible partiality semantics require an authoritative locator.

children.title: Reusable Model Abstractions
children.top_down_role: Encapsulation patterns shared across model components.

assumptions_latex: The abstraction body is well typed and refers only to its parameters and declarations visible at its definition.
Every call satisfies the declared parameter interface.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Replacing each call by a capture-avoiding instance of its body preserves the represented constraints, objective values, and output values.
review_flags: Authoritative MiniZinc specification locator required for scoping and declaration-equivalence qualifications.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extensional reuse through typed MiniZinc predicates and functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A(u_1,\ldots,u_k)\) be the body of a well-formed predicate or function declaration. For compatible actual arguments \((a_1,\ldots,a_k)\), the call's extensional meaning is the capture-avoiding instance \(A[u_i:=a_i]_{i=1}^k\). Consequently, introducing the declaration and replacing repeated compatible instances by calls preserves the model's solution relation and, for functions, the denoted result expressions. This equivalence concerns model meaning; flattening, propagation strength, search order, and runtime may still depend on compiler and solver treatment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Typed predicates and functions can replace repeated model fragments without changing their extensional meaning, although compilation and solver performance may change.
knowledge_statements.title: Reusable Model Abstractions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle kind fits, but unrestricted capture-avoiding expansion and preservation of solutions, objectives, and output values are language-semantic claims needing specification support and qualifications.

children.title: Abstraction Boundary Failures
children.top_down_role: Scoping, typing, or flattening problems at abstraction boundaries.

assumptions_latex: A predicate or function declaration is used as a model abstraction.
Calls are checked against its declared interface and lexical scope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Violation of typing, binding, overload, or total-definition requirements prevents a valid abstraction instance or changes its intended meaning.
review_flags: Authoritative MiniZinc specification locator required for exact static-error and undefinedness categories.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Static and semantic failures of MiniZinc abstraction interfaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a declared abstraction \(A(u_1,\ldots,u_k)\), a call \(A(a_1,\ldots,a_k)\) fails its abstraction boundary if an actual argument is incompatible with its formal parameter, overload resolution is absent or ambiguous, the body contains an unbound identifier, or the declared result cannot be produced on an admissible call. The first three mechanisms prevent a unique well-typed instance. A partial or undefined body can instead make evaluation fail for particular admissible arguments. Hiding such a defect behind a declaration does not make the resulting model fragment valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An abstraction fails when its interface cannot be typed or resolved, its body captures invalid names, or an admissible call has no defined result.
knowledge_statements.title: Abstraction Boundary Failures

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits, but the distinction among static errors, ambiguous overloads, invalid binding, partiality, and evaluation failure is MiniZinc-specific and unsupported.

assumptions_latex: Each library global has a declared MiniZinc interface and a specified relation or function.
Every library call is well typed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Posting a global predicate call restricts assignments to its specified relation; using a global function call denotes its specified result.

notation.meaning: specified relation of a predicate global

review_flags: Authoritative MiniZinc library documentation locator required for the library contract and individual global semantics.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extensional role of MiniZinc library globals in finite-domain models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The global constraint library is a collection of typed predicate and function declarations with specified meanings. For a predicate global \(g\) with relation \(R_g\), posting \(g(a)\) requires \(a\in R_g\). For a function global, \(g(a)\) denotes the value specified by its library contract. A backend may implement a global through a dedicated propagator or an equivalent decomposition. Such implementation choices may change propagation and runtime, but a conforming implementation must preserve the specified relation or function on arguments within the declared interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A global library call denotes a specified typed relation or function, whether the backend uses a dedicated propagator or an equivalent decomposition.
knowledge_statements.title: Global Constraint Library

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind is reasonable for this topic, but the global-library contract and equivalence between dedicated propagators and decompositions need MiniZinc library documentation with specific locators.

children.title: Search Annotations
children.top_down_role: Annotations controlling variable choice, value choice, and search composition.

assumptions_latex: The annotated solve item has a well-defined feasible set and, when applicable, objective.
The search annotation is recognized as an operational search directive rather than an added constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A conforming search annotation may change exploration order and termination behavior but not which complete assignments satisfy the model.
review_flags: Authoritative MiniZinc specification locator required for standard search annotation signatures and completeness parameters.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational directives attached to MiniZinc solve items.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A search annotation \(\alpha\) is an annotation term attached to a solve item that supplies operational choices such as the decision sequence \((x_1,\ldots,x_n)\), variable selection, value selection, or search completeness. It does not add a logical constraint. If the annotated search is complete, solving must enumerate or optimize over the same solution set \(S\) as the unannotated model, subject to the requested solve mode. An incomplete search directive may terminate without establishing infeasibility or global optimality, according to its declared operational contract.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A search annotation guides variable and value exploration without adding constraints; only a complete search can support exhaustive infeasibility or optimality conclusions.
knowledge_statements.title: Search Annotations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits, but the claimed operational fields, nonlogical effect, completeness semantics, and consequences for infeasibility and optimality require specification citations.

children.title: Solver Annotations
children.top_down_role: Annotations interpreted by particular solvers or backend families.

assumptions_latex: An annotation is attached at a syntactically permitted MiniZinc annotation position.
Its arguments satisfy the annotation declaration selected by type checking.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The annotation supplies backend metadata according to its declared contract and has no additional logical effect unless that contract explicitly defines one.

notation.meaning: logical solutions of the underlying model

review_flags: Authoritative MiniZinc specification locator required for annotation declaration, attachment, and backend-handling semantics.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Typed metadata communicated from a MiniZinc model to a backend.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A solver annotation is a well-typed annotation term \(\alpha\) attached to a permitted model item or expression \(M\) to communicate nonlogical information to a compiler or solver. Its recognized meaning is fixed by the annotation's declaration and backend contract, for example selecting an implementation or configuring search. When \(\alpha\) is purely operational, semantic correctness requires \(\operatorname{Sol}(M::\alpha)=\operatorname{Sol}(M)\), although runtime, propagation, solution order, or completeness guarantees may differ. Unsupported or backend-specific annotations need not have portable operational behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A solver annotation is typed backend metadata. Purely operational annotations preserve model solutions but may change propagation, search, runtime, or completeness behavior.
knowledge_statements.title: Solver Annotations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits, but the blanket characterization as nonlogical backend metadata and the solution-preservation equation depend on each annotation’s declared contract and require authoritative support.

children.title: Annotation Portability
children.top_down_role: Transfer of annotation intent across supported solver backends.

assumptions_latex: Two backends accept the same well-typed model and annotation.
The annotation's documented contract is purely operational and both backends implement that contract conformingly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The logical feasible set and objective are portable, while search order, propagation, runtime, and intermediate solutions need not be identical.

notation.meaning: solutions reported by backend b under complete solving

review_flags: Authoritative MiniZinc specification locator required to distinguish mandatory, optional, and backend-specific annotation support.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic versus operational portability of MiniZinc annotations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(b_1\) and \(b_2\) be conforming backends that accept a model \(M\) annotated by a purely operational annotation \(\alpha\), and suppose both runs use complete solving. Annotation portability at the semantic level means \(S_{b_1}(M::\alpha)=S_{b_2}(M::\alpha)=\operatorname{Sol}(M)\), with equal optimal objective values in optimization mode. This equality does not require the backends to use the same algorithm, visit assignments in the same order, return the same first solution, or exhibit comparable propagation and runtime. Backend-specific operational effects are therefore not generally portable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Across conforming complete backends, an operational annotation preserves solutions and optimal values, but its search order and performance effects may differ.
knowledge_statements.title: Annotation Portability

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits, but cross-backend equality of solution sets and optimal values, including the meaning of conforming support, needs precise specification and backend documentation.

children.title: Annotation Degradation
children.top_down_role: Ignored, weakened, or unsupported annotation behavior.

assumptions_latex: The underlying model is valid without the annotation.
The annotation is intended to affect search or implementation rather than impose a logical constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Loss of annotation support can preserve extensional model meaning while weakening operational guarantees; incomplete fallback can also invalidate exhaustive conclusions.
review_flags: Authoritative MiniZinc specification and backend documentation required for unsupported-annotation and fallback behavior.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure modes when a backend cannot realize annotation intent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Annotation degradation occurs when a backend rejects \(\alpha\), ignores it, replaces it by a weaker supported directive, or implements only part of its operational contract. If \(\alpha\) is purely operational and the fallback search remains complete, degradation may still satisfy \(\operatorname{Sol}(M::\alpha)=\operatorname{Sol}(M)\), while losing intended search order or performance. If the replacement is incomplete, a finite run that finds no solution does not certify infeasibility, and a returned incumbent does not certify global optimality unless an independent bound closes the gap. Rejection instead prevents model execution entirely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unsupported annotations may be rejected, ignored, or weakened; semantic solutions can survive complete fallback, but performance and exhaustive conclusions may not.
knowledge_statements.title: Annotation Degradation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits, but rejection, ignoring, weakening, partial implementation, and completeness behavior are backend-dependent and cannot be established without specification and backend sources.

children.title: Output Expressions
children.top_down_role: Model expressions used to construct textual or structured output.

assumptions_latex: An output item contains a well-typed expression whose result is an array of strings.
A solution supplies values for every decision expression evaluated by the output expression.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For each reported solution, evaluating and concatenating the resulting strings determines its rendered textual output without constraining that solution.
review_flags: Authoritative MiniZinc specification locator required for output-item typing, evaluation timing, and absent-value rendering.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-solution evaluation of MiniZinc output expressions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An output expression \(E\) is the expression of a MiniZinc output item and must evaluate to an array of strings. For a reported solution assignment \(s\), the renderer evaluates \(\llbracket E\rrbracket_s\) using the parameter values and the decision values supplied by \(s\), then emits the component strings in index order. Conversions such as displaying a value are expression-level rendering operations. The output item is observational: changing \(E\) may change the text produced for \(s\), but it does not add constraints, alter the objective, or change whether \(s\) is a model solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An output expression evaluates to ordered strings for each reported solution and controls only rendering, not feasibility or objective values.
knowledge_statements.title: Output Expressions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits, but output-item type, evaluation timing, component ordering, absent-value handling, and observational semantics require a specific MiniZinc specification locator.

children.title: Solution Rendering
children.top_down_role: Presentation of assignments, objective values, and derived values.

knowledge_statements.title: Solution Rendering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Denotational view of MiniZinc output evaluation for one solver assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a model, let \(s\) assign values to every decision variable needed by its output item, and let \(E=(e_1,\ldots,e_k)\) be the ordered output expressions. Solution rendering is the partial map \[R_M(s)=\operatorname{concat}\bigl(\operatorname{show}(\llbracket e_1\rrbracket_s),\ldots,\operatorname{show}(\llbracket e_k\rrbracket_s)\bigr).\] It is defined exactly when every \(e_i\) is evaluable under \(s\) and every resulting value admits the requested textual conversion. Rendering observes the assignment but does not alter feasibility or the objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A solution is rendered by evaluating the ordered output expressions under the solver assignment, converting their values to text, and concatenating the results.
assumptions_latex: \(s\) supplies every decision-variable value required by the output expressions.
Each requested conversion is defined for the evaluated value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_M(s)\) is the concatenated textual representation and leaves the solved assignment unchanged.

notation.meaning: value of expression e under assignment s

review_flags: MiniZinc output-semantics source and exact locator required

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation role fits the Solution Rendering leaf, and the statement is internally coherent, but no cited MiniZinc specification supports the asserted partial rendering semantics, conversion boundary, or noninterference claim.

children.title: Multiple-Solution Views
children.top_down_role: Presentation across successive, optimal, or complete solution streams.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiple-Solution Views
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rendering a finite stream of MiniZinc solutions without changing individual assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=(s_1,\ldots,s_m)\) be the ordered solutions emitted by a solver and let \(R_M\) be the model's single-solution renderer. A multiple-solution view is represented by \[V_M(S)=R_M(s_1)\,\delta\,R_M(s_2)\,\delta\cdots\delta\,R_M(s_m)\,\tau,\] where \(\delta\) is the solution separator and \(\tau\) is an optional termination marker determined by the execution interface. Reordering, filtering, or truncating \(S\) changes the view but not the feasibility or values of any retained solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multiple-solution view renders each emitted assignment separately, preserves solver order, and inserts interface-defined separators and an optional termination marker.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is a finite ordered sequence of emitted solutions.
\(R_M(s_i)\) is defined for every retained solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V_M(S)\) preserves the order and individual rendering of all retained solutions.

notation.meaning: ordered sequence of emitted solver assignments
solution separator and optional termination marker

review_flags: MiniZinc solution-stream protocol source and exact locator required

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation role fits the leaf, but the separator, termination-marker, ordering, filtering, and truncation semantics are interface-specific and have no inspectable citation.

children.title: Output Consistency Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Mismatches between model values and displayed solution content.

knowledge_statements.title: Output Consistency Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between valid output evaluation and undefined or misleading rendering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a solved model \(M\) and assignment \(s\), output consistency holds when every output expression is well typed, depends only on values determined by \(s\), and is evaluated using the same parameter data and index sets as the solved instance. Rendering is undefined if evaluation encounters an absent required value, an out-of-domain operation, or an invalid index. Moreover, textual output alone need not be injective: distinct assignments \(s\ne t\) may satisfy \(R_M(s)=R_M(t)\) whenever the output expressions omit or conflate their differing components.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Output is valid only when all expressions are well typed and evaluable against the solved instance; distinct solutions may still render identically if differences are omitted.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) has been instantiated with fixed parameter data.
\(s\) is a solver-returned assignment for that instance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Failure of evaluability makes rendering undefined, while \(s\ne t\) does not imply \(R_M(s)\ne R_M(t)\).

notation.meaning: rendering map induced by the model output item

review_flags: Exact MiniZinc output error and partial-assignment semantics require a normative source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind fits the terminal container, and noninjective rendering is mathematically plausible, but the claimed MiniZinc evaluation failures and consistency conditions require a normative source with a specific locator.

children.title: Type Normalization
children.top_down_role: Canonicalization of type information before backend translation.

knowledge_statements.title: Type Normalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Type-directed normalization preceding generation of a typed flat constraint model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a well-typed model expression \(e:T\). Recursively normalize its subexpressions; resolve overloaded operators from their inferred argument types; insert only semantics-preserving coercions permitted by the source type system; instantiate polymorphic constructs; and replace structured values by a fixed collection of scalar or solver-supported components. Return \(N_T(e)\) with normalized type \(\nu(T)\). The procedure must maintain a reconstruction map \(\rho_T\) such that, for every admissible environment \(\eta\), \[\rho_T\bigl(\llbracket N_T(e)\rrbracket_\eta\bigr)=\llbracket e\rrbracket_\eta.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Type normalization resolves overloads, inserts permitted coercions, and scalarizes unsupported structured types while retaining a map that reconstructs each original value.
assumptions_latex: \(e:T\) is well typed in the source model.
Every introduced coercion is defined by the source language.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_T(e):\nu(T)\) and reconstruction recovers the source denotation.

notation.meaning: normalized representation of source type T

review_flags: Flattening type rules are system-specific and need a MiniZinc or FlatZinc specification locator

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is an appropriate role for this normalization leaf, but overload resolution, coercion insertion, polymorphic instantiation, scalarization, and the reconstruction invariant are system-specific and unsupported by a cited specification.

children.title: Domain Normalization
children.top_down_role: Canonicalization and refinement of finite-domain representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Domain Normalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-domain transformation with an explicit encoding and decoding invariant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a variable \(x\) with finite source domain \(D\). Choose a solver-supported domain \(D'\), an injective encoding \(\epsilon:D\to D'\), and a decoding map \(\delta:\epsilon(D)\to D\). Replace \(x\) by a normalized variable \(x'\in D'\), add the restriction \(x'\in\epsilon(D)\) when \(D'\) is a strict superset, and rewrite each occurrence of \(x\) through the encoding. Output the transformed model together with \(\delta\), satisfying \[\delta(\epsilon(d))=d\qquad\text{for every }d\in D.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Domain normalization encodes each finite source-domain value in a supported domain, restricts the encoded variable, and retains an inverse decoding map.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is finite.
The target language can express \(x'\in\epsilon(D)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Normalized assignments correspond bijectively to source values through \(\epsilon\) and \(\delta\).
review_flags: Specific MiniZinc flattening encodings and domain restrictions need an authoritative locator

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional encoding algorithm is coherent and fits Domain Normalization, but no authoritative locator establishes that this calculus describes the relevant MiniZinc-to-FlatZinc normalization process.

children.title: Expression Normalization
children.top_down_role: Canonical expression forms used by subsequent flattening stages.

assumptions_latex: \(e\) is well typed and defined under every source environment under consideration.
Each defining relation \(D_g\) exactly represents its source operator on admissible arguments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every admissible source environment \(\eta\), a satisfying extension \(\eta'\) exists, and every satisfying extension obeys \(\llbracket e\rrbracket_\eta=\llbracket v\rrbracket_{\eta'}\).

notation.meaning: normalized value and generated constraint conjunction
flat defining relation for operator g
source valuation and its extension to fresh variables

review_flags: Exact target grammar and context-sensitive flattening rules require a specification source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Introduction of flat expressions and constraints by recursive, context-sensitive rewriting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a well-typed expression \(e\), recursively normalize its operands and return a pair \((v,C)\), where \(v\) is a target-supported literal, variable, or flat call and \(C\) is a conjunction of generated constraints. A nonflat subexpression \(g(e_1,\ldots,e_k)\) may be replaced by a fresh variable \(y\) and a defining constraint \(D_g(y,v_1,\ldots,v_k)\). For every admissible environment \(\eta\) over the source variables for which \(e\) is defined, there must exist an extension \(\eta'\) assigning all fresh variables such that \(\eta'\models C\); moreover, every such extension must satisfy \[\llbracket e\rrbracket_\eta=\llbracket v\rrbracket_{\eta'}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expression normalization recursively replaces nested expressions by flat terms and introduces fresh variables with exact defining constraints; every source valuation has a satisfying extension, and every satisfying extension gives the returned flat value the original expression's value.
knowledge_statements.title: Expression Normalization

children.title: Normalization Preservation
children.top_down_role: Preservation of model meaning across normalization transformations.

knowledge_statements.title: Normalization Preservation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solution preservation under type, domain, and expression normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a finite-domain source model and \(N(M)\) its normalized model. Suppose every type transformation has a correct reconstruction map, every domain encoding is injective on admissible values, and every generated defining constraint is exact for its source expression. If \(X\) denotes the source variables and \(Y\) the introduced variables, then \[\operatorname{Sol}(M)=\{\rho(s|_X):s\in\operatorname{Sol}(N(M))\},\] and every \(t\in\operatorname{Sol}(M)\) has at least one extension \(s\in\operatorname{Sol}(N(M))\) with \(\rho(s|_X)=t\). For optimization models, corresponding solutions have equal objective values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under exact encodings and defining constraints, normalized solutions project and decode to precisely the source solutions, with objective values preserved.
assumptions_latex: All type and domain encodings admit correct reconstruction on admissible values.
Every introduced defining constraint is equivalent to its source expression.
The objective is rewritten by the same normalization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Decoded projection gives exactly \(\operatorname{Sol}(M)\), and corresponding objective values agree.
review_flags: Formal normalization-correctness theorem and system-specific hypotheses need a source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem kind correctly fits Normalization Preservation, but the combined reconstruction map, exact solution correspondence, extension property, and objective preservation depend on system-specific normalization rules for which no source is supplied.

children.title: Auxiliary Variables
children.top_down_role: Introduced variables used to represent flattened subexpressions.

knowledge_statements.title: Auxiliary Variables
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fresh variables introduced to name intermediate expressions during flattening.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M(X)\) be a source model with variable set \(X\). A variable \(y\notin X\) is an auxiliary variable of a flattened model \(F(X,Y)\) if it is introduced by the transformation rather than declared by the source model and occurs in constraints connecting it to source variables or earlier auxiliaries. The auxiliary set is \(Y=\operatorname{vars}(F)\setminus X\). It is semantically hidden: solutions of interest are obtained by projection onto \(X\), possibly followed by decoding of normalized domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An auxiliary variable is a fresh, transformation-introduced variable used to name an intermediate value and omitted when flattened solutions are projected back to source variables.
assumptions_latex: Source and generated variable identities are distinct.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Y=\operatorname{vars}(F)\setminus X\), and auxiliaries are eliminated from reported source solutions by projection.
review_flags: A flattening-specific authoritative definition and locator are required

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Definition fits the Auxiliary Variables leaf and is plausible, but the identification of every generated variable with \(\operatorname{vars}(F)\setminus X\) and its projection semantics require a flattening-specific source.

children.title: Defining Constraints
children.top_down_role: Constraints linking introduced variables to source-level expressions.

knowledge_statements.title: Defining Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraints that link an auxiliary variable exactly to its originating expression.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(e(X,Z)\) be a source subexpression and let \(y\) be a fresh auxiliary variable. A constraint \(D_e(y,X,Z)\) is defining for \(y\) when, for every admissible assignment \(a\) to \(X\cup Z\), \[D_e(y,a)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad y=\llbracket e\rrbracket_a.\] More generally, under an encoding \(\epsilon\), the right-hand side is \(y=\epsilon(\llbracket e\rrbracket_a)\). Thus existence of \(y\) does not remove any source assignment, and projecting satisfying extensions onto the source variables restores the original relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A defining constraint forces a fresh auxiliary variable to equal the value, or encoded value, of the source subexpression it names.
assumptions_latex: \(e\) is defined for every admissible assignment considered.
\(y\) is fresh.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_e\) is exact in both directions and preserves source assignments under projection.

notation.meaning: defining constraint for source expression e

review_flags: Locator may discuss modeling definitions rather than flattening-introduced defining constraints

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Definition is the correct content kind, but the Williams locator appears to concern modeling-level defining constraints and does not establish the stated flattening-specific biconditional, encoded variant, or projection-preservation conclusion. A directly supporting source is required.

children.title: Auxiliary Dependency Structure
children.top_down_role: Dependency patterns among introduced variables and flattened constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Auxiliary Dependency Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directed dependency graph induced by auxiliary definitions in a flattened model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For auxiliary variables \(Y\), define the directed graph \(G=(Y,E)\) by \((u,v)\in E\) exactly when the defining constraint for \(v\) uses \(u\). Source variables are external inputs and may be added as root vertices. If auxiliaries are introduced by a recursive traversal without cyclic definitions, their creation order is a topological order of \(G\). In that case auxiliary values can be reconstructed successively from source values. Shared subexpressions may be represented by a single vertex with multiple outgoing dependency uses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Auxiliary definitions form a directed graph: an edge points from an auxiliary used in another auxiliary's definition to the dependent auxiliary.
assumptions_latex: Each auxiliary has an identified defining constraint.
Dependencies are determined from variables occurring in those definitions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If definitions are acyclic, \(G\) has a topological order permitting successive auxiliary reconstruction.

notation.meaning: the definition of v uses auxiliary u

review_flags: Acyclicity depends on the flattening procedure and needs system-specific evidence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The graph is appropriately classified as a representation, but creation order, acyclicity, reconstructibility, and shared-subexpression handling depend on the concrete flattening procedure and lack an inspectable source.

children.title: Auxiliary Proliferation
children.top_down_role: Model growth caused by excessive auxiliary-variable introduction.

knowledge_statements.title: Auxiliary Proliferation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Size growth from naming nonflat expression occurrences during flattening.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(|M|\) be the number of nodes in the source model's expanded expression syntax, and suppose flattening introduces at most one auxiliary variable and at most \(c\) defining constraints for each nonflat node, where \(c\) is constant. Then the numbers of introduced auxiliaries and defining constraints satisfy \[|Y|\le |M|\qquad\text{and}\qquad |C_{\mathrm{def}}|\le c|M|.\] This linear bound applies to the already expanded representation. If comprehensions, indexed declarations, or function calls are unfolded first, \(|M|\) itself may be exponentially larger than the compact source text.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Naming each expanded nonflat expression introduces only linearly many auxiliaries and defining constraints, but prior unfolding can make the expanded model exponentially larger.
assumptions_latex: At most one auxiliary is introduced per expanded nonflat expression node.
Each auxiliary generates at most a constant number \(c\) of defining constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|Y|=O(|M|)\) and \(|C_{\mathrm{def}}|=O(|M|)\), measured after expansion.

notation.meaning: node count of the expanded source expression syntax

review_flags: Bound is conditional on the stated flattening policy; a complexity source is required

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity_bound kind exactly fits the terminal container, and the linear inequalities follow conditionally from the stated counting assumptions. However, applicability to the intended flattener and the claim of possible exponential growth during unfolding require a specific complexity source.

knowledge_statements.title: Native Global Preservation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Retaining recognized global constraints as native target-language calls during flattening.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G(x_1,\ldots,x_k)\) be a source global constraint and let \(g\) be a target solver's native constraint with the same relation after argument encoding. Native global preservation replaces the source occurrence by the single call \(g(\epsilon_1(x_1),\ldots,\epsilon_k(x_k))\), adding only constraints required by the encodings. The replacement is admissible when, for every admissible tuple \(a\), \[G(a)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad g(\epsilon_1(a_1),\ldots,\epsilon_k(a_k)).\] Otherwise the global must be redefined or decomposed rather than claimed as preserved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A global constraint is preserved natively only when the target solver call represents exactly the same relation after argument encoding.
assumptions_latex: The target backend declares a native relation \(g\).
Each argument encoding \(\epsilon_i\) is defined on its admissible source domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact relational equivalence permits one native call; absent equivalence, native preservation is invalid.
review_flags: Native-global mapping and equivalence obligations require MiniZinc and backend specification sources

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Principle is an appropriate role for Native Global Preservation, and exact relational equivalence is the right abstract obligation. No MiniZinc or backend specification is cited to support native mapping behavior or the claimed decomposition boundary.

knowledge_statements.title: Solver-Specific Global Redefinition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Backend-specific replacement of a global finite-domain constraint by an equivalent supported formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G(x)\) be a global constraint over finite-domain variables \(x\), and let backend \(B\) support a predicate \(H_B(x,y)\) with auxiliary variables \(y\). A solver-specific redefinition is valid when
\[G(x)\iff \exists y\in D_y:\ H_B(x,y).\]
Thus the projection onto the source variables of the satisfying assignments of \(H_B\) equals the satisfying assignments of \(G\). If an objective \(f(x)\) is present and does not depend on \(y\), this equivalence also preserves feasible objective values and optimal source assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A global constraint may be replaced by a backend-specific formulation exactly when projecting the replacement's solutions onto source variables recovers the original solutions.
assumptions_latex: \(D_x\) and \(D_y\) are finite domains.
\(H_B\) is accepted by backend \(B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x:G(x)\}=\{x:\exists y\in D_y,\ H_B(x,y)\}\).

notation.meaning: auxiliary variables introduced by the replacement

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation matches the solver-specific redefinition leaf and states the appropriate projected-solution equivalence, including a properly qualified objective-preservation clause. However, no citation or inspectable locator is supplied, so the backend-redefinition criterion lacks the required evidence.

knowledge_statements.title: Global Decomposition During Flattening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact decomposition of a global constraint into primitive constraints during model flattening.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G(x)\) be a global constraint and let \(c_1(x,y),\ldots,c_m(x,y)\) be primitive constraints admitted by the target language. An exact flattening decomposition satisfies
\[G(x)\iff \exists y\in D_y:\bigwedge_{i=1}^{m}c_i(x,y).\]
The flattened constraint set may introduce auxiliary variables, but every original satisfying assignment must admit an auxiliary extension, and every flattened satisfying assignment must project to an original satisfying assignment. Logical equivalence alone does not assert that propagation strength or search behavior is preserved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A global constraint is decomposed exactly when the primitive formulation has precisely the same projected solutions, though its propagation may differ.
assumptions_latex: \(x\) and \(y\) have finite domains.
Each \(c_i\) belongs to the target primitive language.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_x\{(x,y):\bigwedge_i c_i(x,y)\}=\{x:G(x)\}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation correctly distinguishes exact projected-solution decomposition from preservation of propagation strength and fits this leaf. No source reference or specific locator supports the characterization of global-constraint decomposition during flattening.

children.title: Single-Pass Simplification
children.top_down_role: Local reductions performed during one traversal of the model.

knowledge_statements.title: Single-Pass Simplification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One traversal applying local, semantics-preserving simplifications without revisiting transformed nodes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a finite expression tree \(E\), an ordered family \(S\) of semantics-preserving simplification rules, and a fixed traversal order, visit every original node exactly once. At a visited node \(v\), apply the first rule in \(S\) whose left-hand side matches the current subtree; replace that subtree by the instantiated right-hand side and do not revisit the replacement. If no rule matches, retain the subtree. After the traversal, output \(E'\). Each applied rule must satisfy \(\llbracket l\sigma\rrbracket=\llbracket r\sigma\rrbracket\), hence \(\llbracket E'\rrbracket=\llbracket E\rrbracket\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Visit each original expression node once, apply the first matching valid simplification, and never revisit its replacement; the resulting expression remains semantically equivalent.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) is a finite expression tree.
Every rule in \(S\) preserves denotation on its applicability domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\llbracket E'\rrbracket=\llbracket E\rrbracket\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm is internally coherent under its stated convention, but 'visit every original node exactly once' and the treatment of replaced subtrees are convention-dependent. No authoritative rewriting or flattening source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Single-Pass Rewriting
children.top_down_role: Expression substitutions performed within one flattening pass.

knowledge_statements.title: Single-Pass Rewriting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic ordered rewriting of a model intermediate representation in one traversal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a finite intermediate-representation tree and \(R=(r_1,\ldots,r_k)\) an ordered rule list. Traverse the nodes existing when their parent is visited according to a fixed order. At each node, select the least \(i\) for which \(r_i\) matches, replace the matched subtree once, record any generated declarations or constraints, and continue without returning to that replacement. Emit the rewritten model \(T_R(M)\) after the traversal. The transformation is deterministic when traversal order, rule priority, matching, and fresh-name generation are deterministic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A single-pass rewriter traverses a model once, applies the highest-priority matching rule at each node, and does not reconsider generated replacements.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is finite.
Rule matching and fresh-name generation are deterministic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_R(M)\) is uniquely determined by \(M\), \(R\), and the traversal order.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the appropriate content kind, but the phrase 'nodes existing when their parent is visited' does not fully determine which descendants survive replacement or are subsequently visited. An authoritative source is required to establish the intended single-pass operational semantics.

children.title: Rewrite Ordering Effects
children.top_down_role: Sensitivity of flattened forms to transformation ordering.

knowledge_statements.title: Rewrite Ordering Effects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Noncommutativity and priority sensitivity of overlapping rewrite rules in a single pass.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(r\) and \(s\) be semantics-preserving rewrite rules applicable to overlapping parts of some model \(M\). If one application disables or changes the match of the other, then their single-pass transformations need not commute:
\[T_{(r,s)}(M)\ne T_{(s,r)}(M),\]
even though both outputs may remain semantically equivalent to \(M\). Consequently, rule priority can change the number of auxiliary variables, the primitive constraints emitted, and which later simplifications become applicable. Semantic preservation therefore does not imply representation independence under rule reordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Overlapping valid rewrite rules can produce different equivalent flat models when reordered, affecting auxiliaries, emitted constraints, and later simplification opportunities.
assumptions_latex: \(r\) and \(s\) preserve semantics individually.
Their matches overlap and at least one application changes the other's applicability.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_{(r,s)}(M)\) and \(T_{(s,r)}(M)\) may be syntactically distinct while denoting the same source model.

notation.meaning: single-pass transformation with r prioritized before s

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is appropriately a property of rewrite ordering, and the modal conclusion is plausible. The stated overlap condition alone does not demonstrate noncommutativity for a given pair of rules, and no cited example or rewriting-system source with a locator is provided.

children.title: Single-Pass Limitations
children.top_down_role: Optimization opportunities unavailable without later model information.

knowledge_statements.title: Single-Pass Limitations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of one nonrevisiting traversal to compute a rewrite normal form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the semantics-preserving rule \(r:u+0\to u\) and the expression \(E=(x+0)+0\). A root-first single-pass rewriter that applies \(r\) at the root and does not revisit the replacement outputs \(x+0\), although \(r\) remains applicable. Thus one pass need not produce a normal form. More generally, whenever a rewrite creates a new match at an already visited position, a nonrevisiting transformation can miss that match; iteration, work-list scheduling, or an additional pass is required to guarantee saturation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonrevisiting pass can leave newly exposed rewrites unapplied; for example, simplifying the root of (x+0)+0 may leave x+0.
assumptions_latex: Replacements are not revisited.
Traversal is root-first for the displayed example.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_r((x+0)+0)=x+0\) and \(x+0\) is not \(r\)-normal.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample correctly shows that the specified root-first, nonrevisiting pass need not reach normal form, and failure_boundary is the exact role for this leaf. Nevertheless, the record contains no citation or inspectable locator, as required for candidate-review knowledge.

children.title: Two-Pass Flattening
children.top_down_role: Flattening regimes that revisit an intermediate model.

knowledge_statements.title: Two-Pass Flattening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Analysis followed by coordinated emission of a finite-domain flat model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a source model \(M	o\min f(x)\) and backend capability description \(K_B\), pass one traverses \(M\) to infer domains, collect global-constraint occurrences, compute use counts, and attach representation candidates and semantic identifiers, producing annotations \(A\). Pass two traverses \((M,A)\), selects an encoding supported by \(K_B\) for each annotated construct, introduces fresh auxiliaries, and emits a flat model \(F_B(M)\). It returns both the flat model and a projection map \(\pi\). Output is accepted only if feasible assignments extend and project through \(\pi\) without changing \(f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The first pass gathers model-wide information; the second selects supported encodings and emits a flat model with a source-variable projection map.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) has finite variable domains.
Every selected encoding is exact and supported by \(K_B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi(\operatorname{Feas}(F_B(M)))=\operatorname{Feas}(M)\) and source objective values are preserved.

notation.meaning: projection from flat to source assignments

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm fits the leaf, but the particular first-pass annotations and second-pass responsibilities describe a specific architecture without evidence. The source model notation fixes minimization while the conclusion uses generic objective preservation, and no authoritative two-pass flattening source is cited.

children.title: Backend-Aware Flattening
children.top_down_role: Transformations specialized to backend capabilities or vocabularies.

knowledge_statements.title: Backend-Aware Flattening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Capability-guided selection among exact flat encodings for a designated solver backend.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each source constraint \(c\), let \(\mathcal E(c)\) be candidate encodings and let \(K_B\) describe the primitives and native globals supported by backend \(B\). Select
\[e_B(c)\in\arg\min\{\kappa_B(e):e\in\mathcal E(c),\ e\subseteq K_B,\ e\equiv c\},\]
where \(\kappa_B\) is a backend-specific encoding cost. Introduce the auxiliaries required by each selected encoding and emit their conjunction. If the feasible set in braces is empty, report unsupported rather than emit an inexact encoding. The resulting flat model is backend-aware but remains semantically equivalent under projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose the least-cost exact encoding supported by the target backend; if none exists, report the construct as unsupported.
assumptions_latex: Candidate encodings have decidable support and exactness metadata.
\(\kappa_B\) totally orders tied candidates by a deterministic rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(e_B(c)\equiv c\) for every emitted source-constraint encoding.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Backend-aware encoding selection is appropriately presented as an algorithm. However, the relation e subseteq K_B is not formally typed when e is an encoding and K_B a vocabulary, and the argmin cost-selection model is a design choice requiring a source. No citation or locator is supplied.

children.title: Cross-Pass Coordination
children.top_down_role: Information transfer between successive flattening passes.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Pass Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency conditions linking analysis annotations to decisions made in a later flattening pass.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let pass one assign each source construct \(c\) an annotation \(A(c)\) containing its inferred domain, occurrence identifier, and admissible encodings. Pass two must select and emit an encoding using the same annotation: for every introduced auxiliary \(y\), its declared domain must contain every value permitted by the selected encoding, and every emitted constraint must retain the occurrence identifier of \(c\). If pass two invalidates an inference in \(A(c)\), the affected analysis must be recomputed or the transformation rejected; silently using inconsistent annotations does not establish semantic preservation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Later flattening decisions must respect earlier domains, encoding choices, and source identifiers; invalidated analysis must be recomputed or rejected.
assumptions_latex: Pass-one annotations are sound when created.
Pass two can detect annotation precondition violations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall c,\ \operatorname{pre}(e(c))\subseteq A(c)\) and every emitted object is traceable to its source occurrence.

notation.meaning: analysis annotation for source construct c
information required to justify encoding e

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Principle is a suitable role, but the conclusion pre(e(c)) subseteq A(c) treats an annotation record as a set without defining the containment relation and does not capture all domain and traceability conditions stated in prose. The proposed cross-pass invariant also has no authoritative source.

children.title: Backend Portability Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Loss of portability caused by backend-specific transformations.

knowledge_statements.title: Backend Portability Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact portability is limited by the common expressible fragment or available backend-specific decompositions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For backends \(B_1,\ldots,B_q\) with supported vocabularies \(K_{B_i}\), a single unchanged flat model is directly portable only if every emitted constraint lies in
\[K_{\mathrm{common}}=\bigcap_{i=1}^{q}K_{B_i}.\]
A source construct outside this intersection remains portably flattenable only when, for every backend, an exact encoding into that backend's vocabulary is available. If some backend lacks both native support and an exact finite encoding, semantics-preserving portability to that backend fails. Backend-specific performance properties, including propagation strength, need not be portable even when solution-set equivalence is.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Direct portability requires common supported primitives; otherwise every backend needs an exact encoding, and equivalent encodings may still propagate differently.
assumptions_latex: Each \(K_{B_i}\) precisely describes backend support.
Portability requires exact projected solution sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c\notin K_{B_j}\) with no exact \(K_{B_j}\)-encoding implies that \(c\) is not semantics-preservingly portable to \(B_j\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits, and the distinction between unchanged-model portability, backend-specific exact encodings, and propagation behavior is mathematically sensible. The vocabulary-intersection model and impossibility condition lack a supporting source with a specific locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Semantic Preservation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected solution and objective preservation under finite-domain model flattening.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let source model \(M\) have variables \(x\), feasible set \(S\), and objective \(f(x)\). Let its flat model \(F\\) have variables \((x,y)\), feasible set \(S_F\), and objective \(f_F(x,y)\). Flattening is semantics-preserving when
\[S=\operatorname{proj}_x(S_F)\quad\text{and}\quad f_F(x,y)=f(x)\ \text{for all }(x,y)\in S_F.\]
For satisfaction models, the second condition is omitted. For optimization models these conditions imply equality of attainable objective values and equality, after projection, of optimal source assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Flattening preserves semantics when flat solutions project exactly to source solutions and retain the source objective value.
assumptions_latex: All source and auxiliary domains are finite.
The flat model retains the source variables or an explicit decoding of them.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_x(\operatorname{Argopt}F)=\operatorname{Argopt}M\) and \(\operatorname{opt}(F)=\operatorname{opt}(M)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Property is the correct role and projected feasible-set plus objective-value preservation captures the intended local concept. However, statement_latex contains the malformed token F\\, and Argopt is used without specifying minimization or maximization. Because no authoritative source is supplied to settle the intended formulation, the record requires sourcing before mathematical revision.

knowledge_statements.title: Source-to-Flat Model Mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Traceability maps connecting source entities, generated flat entities, and assignment decoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A source-to-flat mapping for a source model \(M\) and flat model \(F\) is a pair \((\tau,\delta)\). For every source occurrence \(a\), \(\tau(a)\) is the nonempty set of flat variables and constraints generated wholly or partly from \(a\). For every feasible flat assignment \(z\), \(\delta(z)\) is a source assignment satisfying
\[\delta(z)(x)=\llbracket e_x\rrbracket_z\]
for a recorded flat expression \(e_x\) associated with each source variable \(x\). Traceability is complete when every generated flat entity has at least one source antecedent and decoding is defined for every feasible flat assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Traceability records which flat entities arise from each source occurrence and how every feasible flat assignment decodes to source-variable values.
assumptions_latex: Every source variable has a recorded decoding expression.
Generated identifiers are stable within the flattening run.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall z\in\operatorname{Feas}(F),\ \delta(z)\in\operatorname{Feas}(M)\), with complete antecedent coverage of generated entities.

notation.meaning: flat expression representing source variable x

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation fits the source-to-flat mapping leaf, but provenance completeness and decoding do not by themselves imply that every decoded assignment is feasible for the source model; that semantic condition must be included explicitly or derived from a cited flattening-correctness result. No source or locator is provided.

children.title: FlatZinc Textual Representation
children.top_down_role: Concrete textual structure of FlatZinc models.

knowledge_statements.title: FlatZinc Textual Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract characterization of a flattened model serialized in FlatZinc concrete syntax.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A textual FlatZinc representation of a flattened constraint model is a finite token sequence parsed as a tuple \(T=(P,D,C,S,O)\), where \(P\) contains parameter declarations, \(D\) contains variable declarations with finite or primitive domains, \(C\) is an ordered list of primitive constraint applications, \(S\) is one solve item, and \(O\) contains output annotations or expressions. Every identifier used by \(C\), \(S\), or \(O\) must be declared in \(P\cup D\); every constraint argument must have the primitive type required by its predicate signature; and \(S\) specifies satisfaction, minimization, or maximization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: FlatZinc text serializes declarations, primitive constraints, one solve directive, and output instructions, subject to declaration, typing, and predicate-signature consistency.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is accepted by the applicable FlatZinc grammar.
Predicate signatures and primitive types are fixed by the applicable interface version.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T\) determines a well-typed flattened constraint instance and its requested solve mode.

notation.meaning: Parameters, variable declarations, constraints, solve item, and output component.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the leaf, but the proposed tuple decomposition, domain characterization, output component, and claim that the text determines a well-typed instance are version-dependent FlatZinc assertions with no cited grammar or specification locator. Authoritative source inspection is required before the mathematical statement can be assessed reliably.

children.title: FlatZinc-JSON Representation
children.top_down_role: Structured JSON form of FlatZinc model content.

knowledge_statements.title: FlatZinc-JSON Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract structured-data counterpart of a FlatZinc model; the applicable schema version must be fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A FlatZinc-JSON representation is a JSON value \(J\) conforming to a specified schema \(\Sigma\), with structured fields encoding parameters, variable declarations, primitive constraint applications, the solve item, and output information. Schema validity requires unique declaration identifiers, references only to declared objects, arguments compatible with predicate signatures, and exactly one solve specification. If \(\operatorname{decode}_{\Sigma}(J)=M\), then \(M\) is the flattened model represented by \(J\); JSON member ordering and insignificant textual formatting do not alter \(M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: FlatZinc-JSON stores the components of a flattened model as schema-governed JSON objects and arrays, with typed references and a single solve specification.
assumptions_latex: A concrete FlatZinc-JSON schema \(\Sigma\) and version are fixed.
\(J\) is valid JSON.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Schema-valid \(J\) decodes to a well-typed flattened model \(M\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the leaf, but no concrete FlatZinc-JSON schema, version, or authoritative source is identified. The asserted fields, uniqueness rules, single-solve requirement, decoding map, and order invariance therefore cannot be distinguished from a hypothetical JSON design.

children.title: Cross-Format Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Element-level correspondence between textual and JSON forms.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Format Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic correspondence between textual and JSON encodings of the same flattened model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) be a valid textual FlatZinc document and \(J\) a schema-valid FlatZinc-JSON value. They correspond exactly when there exists a flattened model \(M\) such that \(\operatorname{parse}(T)=M\) and \(\operatorname{decode}_{\Sigma}(J)=M\), modulo alpha-renaming of identifiers and other explicitly declared representation-neutral normalizations. Equivalently, the two encodings must preserve declaration types and domains, primitive constraint symbols and argument references, solve mode and objective, annotations whose semantics are retained, and output observables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The formats correspond when parsing the text and decoding the JSON produce the same typed model, solve request, retained annotations, and outputs.
assumptions_latex: Both representations are valid under mutually compatible interface versions.
The permitted normalization relation is fixed in advance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T\sim_{a0\Sigma}J\iff \operatorname{parse}(T)\equiv\operatorname{decode}_{\Sigma}(J)\).

notation.meaning: Model equality modulo declared representation-neutral normalizations.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits a correspondence leaf, but an official mapping and normalization policy are absent, so preservation of annotations and outputs cannot be validated. The conclusion also writes \(T\sim_{a0\Sigma}J\), whereas the statement and notation define \(T\sim_{\Sigma}J\). Source uncertainty controls the verdict; the notation defect must also be repaired once the supported correspondence is established.

children.title: Representation Divergence
children.top_down_role: Format-specific omissions, extensions, or interpretation differences.

knowledge_statements.title: Representation Divergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure modes that prevent textual and JSON representations from denoting the same model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Cross-format equivalence fails whenever translation changes a semantically relevant component. Concretely, if \(T\) and \(J\) differ after decoding in any variable domain, primitive predicate or argument, solve mode, objective expression, retained annotation, or observable output, then \(\operatorname{parse}(T)\not\equiv\operatorname{decode}_{\Sigma}(J)\). Divergence can also arise when one format admits a construct that the selected version of the other format cannot encode; any lossy fallback then requires an explicit rejection or a declared approximation contract and cannot be treated as exact correspondence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The representations diverge if conversion alters domains, constraints, objectives, meaningful annotations, or outputs, or if one format cannot encode a required construct.
assumptions_latex: Semantic equality \(\equiv\) includes every component relevant to solving or reported output.
The two format versions and retained-annotation policy are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A mismatch in any preserved component implies \(T\not\sim_{\Sigma}J\).

notation.meaning: The textual and JSON representations do not correspond.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind is appropriate. However, exact semantic equality, retained annotations, cross-version encodability, and the required behavior for lossy fallback depend on format specifications and translation policy that are neither fixed nor cited.

knowledge_statements.title: FlatZinc Primitive Vocabulary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Typed vocabulary available to a flattened model and its solver backend.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an interface version \(v\), the FlatZinc primitive vocabulary is a typed signature \(\mathcal V_v=(\mathcal T_v,\mathcal P_v,\operatorname{sig}_v)\). Here \(\mathcal T_v\) is the set of primitive scalar, set, and array types; \(\mathcal P_v\) is the set of primitive constraint and operation symbols; and \(\operatorname{sig}_v(p)=(\tau_1,\ldots,\tau_k)\) assigns each symbol \(p\) its ordered argument types. A primitive application \(p(a_1,\ldots,a_k)\) is well formed exactly when every \(a_i\) has a type compatible with \(\tau_i\), including required array index and element types.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The primitive vocabulary is the versioned collection of FlatZinc types and primitive symbols together with their ordered argument signatures.
assumptions_latex: A FlatZinc interface version \(v\) is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p(a_1,\ldots,a_k)\) is well formed precisely when its arguments conform to \(\operatorname{sig}_v(p)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the topic, but the proposed signature model and its inclusion of primitive scalar, set, array, constraint, and operation symbols require an official version-specific FlatZinc catalog. With no source locator, the exact vocabulary and compatibility rules cannot be validated.

knowledge_statements.title: Solver-Specific Libraries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Backend extensions that add predicates or annotations beyond the common primitive interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a solver backend \(s\) with common vocabulary \(\mathcal V_v\), a solver-specific library is a versioned extension \(L_s=(P_s,A_s,I_s)\), where \(P_s\) contains additional typed predicate declarations, \(A_s\) contains solver-recognized annotations, and \(I_s\) supplies their backend interpretation or implementation contract. A flattened model may depend on \(L_s\) only if each referenced extension has a declared signature and the selected solver configuration advertises a compatible library version; otherwise the model is not portable to that configuration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A solver-specific library adds typed predicates and annotations with backend meanings; models using them require a solver configuration that advertises a compatible version.
assumptions_latex: The common interface version \(v\) and backend \(s\) are fixed.
Extension names do not ambiguously shadow incompatible common primitives.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A model using \(L_s\) is admissible only when its selected backend supports every referenced extension.

notation.meaning: Extended predicates, annotations, and interpretation contract.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind is reasonable for this topic, but the tuple \(L_s=(P_s,A_s,I_s)\), advertised-version requirement, loading behavior, and portability conclusion are implementation-specific claims unsupported by any cited solver-library specification.

children.title: Solver Configuration
children.top_down_role: Backend selection, invocation, paths, flags, and default settings.

knowledge_statements.title: Solver Configuration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete selection and parameterization of a FlatZinc solver backend.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A solver configuration is a tuple \(K=(s,e,v,L,	heta)\), where \(s\) identifies a solver, \(e\) identifies its executable or invocation mechanism, \(v\) is the supported interface version, \(L\) is the set of enabled solver-specific libraries, and \(\theta\) is a finite map from option names to typed values. The configuration is well formed when the executable is associated with \(s\), every library in \(L\) is loadable by that solver version, and each option value satisfies its declared type and admissible range.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A solver configuration identifies the backend and invocation, interface version, enabled libraries, and typed option values, all subject to compatibility checks.
assumptions_latex: Solver and option identifiers are interpreted relative to a fixed configuration registry.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A well-formed \(K\) specifies one executable backend configuration for processing compatible flattened models.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the leaf, but the five-component configuration tuple and its well-formedness conditions are presented as an interface definition without a configuration registry or schema citation. Actual FlatZinc solver configuration fields and validation rules may differ.

children.title: Capability Metadata
children.top_down_role: Declared backend support for features, formats, and execution modes.

knowledge_statements.title: Capability Metadata
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Machine-readable declaration of what a solver configuration claims to support.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Capability metadata for a solver configuration \(K\) is a finite record \(C_K=(V_K,P_K,L_K,O_K,F_K)
í, where \(V_K\) lists supported interface versions, \(P_K\) lists supported primitive signatures, \(L_K\) lists compatible solver-specific libraries, \(O_K\) gives option names with types and admissible values, and \(F_K\) records supported solve and reporting features. Metadata is internally consistent when every referenced type and version exists, signatures are unambiguous, option domains are nonempty, and each library dependency is declared.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Capability metadata records supported interface versions, primitives, libraries, options, and solve or reporting features for a solver configuration.
assumptions_latex: A metadata schema and interpretation for configuration \(K\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Internally consistent \(C_K\) defines a decidable advertised-support predicate for finite model requirements.

notation.meaning: Capability record associated with configuration K.
Versions, primitives, libraries, options, and features.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits machine-readable capability metadata, but neither the metadata schema nor the asserted fields and decidability claim have authoritative support. In addition, the statement contains the malformed fragment following \(C_K=(V_K,P_K,L_K,O_K,F_K)\) (rendered as “ní”), which must be removed when a sourced replacement is prepared.

children.title: Configuration–Capability Matching
children.top_down_role: Consistency between selected configuration and advertised backend support.

knowledge_statements.title: Configuration–Capability Matching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility predicate comparing model requirements with advertised backend capabilities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R(M)=(v,P,L,O,F)\) be the finite requirements extracted from a flattened model \(M\), and let \(C_K=(V_K,P_K,L_K,O_K,F_K)\) be the capability metadata of configuration \(K\). The match predicate holds exactly when \(v\in V_K\), every required primitive signature belongs to \(P_K\), every required library has a compatible member in \(L_K\), every requested option belongs to its advertised typed domain in \(O_K\), and \(F\subseteq F_K\). A model should be dispatched through \(K\) only when this predicate holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A configuration matches a model when it supports the required interface version, primitive signatures, libraries, option values, and solve or reporting features.
assumptions_latex: Model requirements and capability metadata use the same identifiers and version-ordering rules.
Capability metadata is current and internally consistent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{match}(M,K)\iff v\in V_K\land P\subseteq P_K\land L\preceq L_K\land O\preceq O_K\land F\subseteq F_K\).

notation.meaning: Finite requirement record extracted from model M.
Componentwise compatibility for libraries or typed options.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind is appropriate, but the exact extraction of \(R(M)\), the subset tests, version compatibility, library compatibility, and typed-option relation are interface-specific and uncited. The overloaded relation \(\preceq\) is described only informally and cannot be validated without the governing interface definition.

children.title: Stale Metadata Failures
children.top_down_role: Failures caused by outdated or inaccurate capability declarations.

knowledge_statements.title: Stale Metadata Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: False compatibility decisions caused by capability records that no longer describe the executable backend.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let metadata \(C_K^{(0)}\) advertise support for primitive \(p\), and suppose the executable behind configuration \(K\) is replaced by a version whose actual capability set \(C_K^{(1)}\) omits \(p\), while the stored metadata is not refreshed. For a model \(M\) requiring \(p\), metadata matching yields \(\operatorname{match}_{C_K^{(0)}}(M,K)=\mathrm{true}\), but actual execution cannot implement the required primitive. Thus stale metadata can produce a false-positive dispatch decision. Conversely, metadata omitting a newly supported primitive produces a false negative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Old metadata can accept an unsupported model after a solver downgrade or reject a newly supported model after an upgrade.
assumptions_latex: Dispatch relies on stored metadata rather than querying or validating the active executable.
The active backend capability set differs from the stored capability record.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_K^{(0)}\ne C_K^{(1)}\) can make metadata matching unsound or incomplete relative to actual execution.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample kind correctly describes the explicit stale-metadata construction and fits the failure leaf. Nevertheless, the configuration's metadata lifecycle, replacement behavior, and meaning of actual capability set are interface-specific and have no cited source, so applicability to the target interface remains uncertain.

children.title: Solution Records
children.top_down_role: Backend output carrying assignments and objective values.

knowledge_statements.title: Solution Records
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structured record for one solver-produced assignment and its associated observables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a flattened model with reported variables \(X_{m out}\) and objective expression \(f\) when applicable, a solution record is a tuple \(R=(a,z,o,m)\). The map \(a\) assigns a representable value to every required variable in \(X_{m out}\); \(z=f(a)\) is present for an optimization solution when the objective is reported; \(o\) contains formatted or structured output observables; and \(m\) contains optional per-solution metadata. A record is model-consistent when its assignments satisfy all reported-domain and output-evaluation requirements; feasibility additionally requires extension to an assignment satisfying every model constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A solution record contains reported assignments, any objective value, output observables, and optional metadata, with values consistent with the model and output specification.
assumptions_latex: The model's required output variables and serialization rules are fixed.
Any claim of feasibility is checked against the full flattened model.
